title: Coins and notes
examples: What is a one euro coin worth?
Can I make fifty cent with coins?
If I have two euro, what coins can I use?

explain.say: Money comes as coins and notes. Coins are small and round. Notes are made of paper.
In Ireland we use euro and cent. The cent coins are one, two, five, ten, twenty and fifty cent.
One hundred cent make one euro. There are coins for one euro and two euro.
Notes are for bigger amounts. The notes you see most are five, ten, twenty and fifty euro.
You can make one amount with different coins. Two ten cent coins make twenty cent. One twenty cent coin makes the same amount.
To count coins, start with the biggest coin. Then count on with the smaller coins.

faq.q: Can I use coins and notes together to pay?
faq.a: Yes, you can pay with notes and coins together. For example, a five euro note and two one euro coins make seven euro.
asks: Can I mix coins and notes?
Is it okay to use both?

faq.q: What is the difference between cent and euro?
faq.a: A euro is worth more than a cent. One hundred cent make one euro.
asks: How many pence in a pound?

faq.q: How do I make an amount like fifty cent?
faq.a: You can use different coins. For example, two twenty cent coins and one ten cent coin make fifty cent.

faq.q: If I pay with a ten euro note, what happens?
faq.a: If the price is less than ten euro, the shop gives you change. The change is ten euro take away the price.

faq.q: Are all coins the same colour?
faq.a: No. The one, two and five cent coins are copper coloured. The ten, twenty and fifty cent coins are gold coloured. The one and two euro coins have two colours.
asks: How do I know the value?

facts: One euro is equal to one hundred cent.
Notes are used for larger amounts of money.
Change is the money you get back when you pay more than the price.
